title: Say where you live
goal: Say where you live and where you come from, with the right little word before cities and countries.

drills.explain: vous → habitez (ends in an é sound).
elles → habitent; the -ent is silent, but you hear the z: elles‿habitent.
ils / elles → habitent; the -ent is silent.

items.en: Where do you live? (to a friend)

items.note: Before a masculine country: [[je viens du Maroc]]. Before a vowel: [[je viens d'Inde]].
The city has no article: [[à Québec]] = in Quebec City.
Ends in -e but it's masculine: [[au Mexique]].

example.en: Alex lives in the United States.

blocks.title: At a job fair in Montréal
blocks.context: Olivier and Sofia wait in line. Then Sofia talks to Raj, an older man she doesn't know.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Salut ! Moi, c'est Olivier. Tu habites où ?
lines.en: Hi! I'm Olivier. Where do you live?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Moi, c'est Sofia. J'habite à Laval, mais je viens du Mexique.
lines.en: I'm Sofia. I live in Laval, but I'm from Mexico.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Oui ! Et toi, tu habites à Montréal ?
lines.en: Yes! And you, do you live in Montréal?

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Non, j'habite à Longueuil. Je suis français, je viens de Lyon, en France.
lines.en: No, I live in Longueuil. I'm French, I'm from Lyon, in France.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Bonjour, monsieur. Vous habitez à Montréal aussi ?
lines.en: Hello, sir. Do you live in Montréal too?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Non, j'habite à Québec. Je viens d'Inde.
lines.en: No, I live in Quebec City. I'm from India.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: À Québec ? Alors vous habitez à Québec, au Québec !
lines.en: In Quebec City? So you live in Quebec City, in Quebec!

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Oui, c'est ça ! Et nous habitons tous au Canada.
lines.en: Yes, that's it! And we all live in Canada.

blocks.body: Listen for the small words before places: [[à]], [[en]], [[au]]. They are what this lesson is about.

steps.title: Habiter and the little words for “in”

blocks.title: Habiter means “to live (somewhere)”
blocks.body: [[Habiter]] is a **regular** verb: you keep [[habit-]] and change the ending. The **h is silent**, so the word really starts with a vowel sound. That's why [[je]] becomes [[j']], and why you hear a *z* after [[nous]], [[vous]], [[ils]] and [[elles]].

blocks.title: Habiter in the present
head: habiter
English
rows: you live (formal, or more than one person)
blocks.note: [[habite]], [[habites]] and [[habitent]] sound exactly the same: *a-BEET*. Endings -e, -es and -ent are silent.

blocks.title: In + a place
head: place
in…
English
blocks.note: **City → à. Feminine country → en. Masculine country → au. Plural country → aux.** Most countries ending in **-e** are feminine; [[le Mexique]] is a famous exception.

blocks.title: Saying where you live
blocks.pattern: j'habite + à + city, + en / au / aux + country
blocks.note: You can give the city and the country together, separated by a comma.

examples.en: I live in Toronto, in Canada.

examples.fr: Amira habite à Casablanca, au Maroc.
examples.en: Amira lives in Casablanca, in Morocco.

examples.fr: Nous habitons à Paris, en France.
examples.en: We live in Paris, in France.

blocks.title: Au Québec or à Québec?
blocks.body:
**Québec** is both a province and a city, and the little word tells you which one:

- [[au Québec]] = in the **province** ([[le Québec]] is masculine)
- [[à Québec]] = in **Quebec City** (a city → à)

Most other provinces follow the same rules. Feminine ones and names starting with a vowel take [[en]]: [[en Ontario]], [[en Alberta]], [[en Colombie-Britannique]], [[en Nouvelle-Écosse]]. Masculine ones take [[au]]: [[au Manitoba]], [[au Nouveau-Brunswick]]. Cities always take [[à]]: [[à Moncton]], [[à Gatineau]], [[à Vancouver]].

examples.fr: Lucie habite à Québec, au Québec.
examples.en: Lucie lives in Quebec City, in Quebec.

examples.fr: Karim habite à Ottawa, en Ontario.
examples.en: Karim lives in Ottawa, in Ontario.

examples.fr: Mei habite à Moncton, au Nouveau-Brunswick.
examples.en: Mei lives in Moncton, in New Brunswick.

blocks.title: Je viens de… (where you're from)
blocks.body:
[[Je viens de…]] means “I come from…”. The verb [[venir]] comes later; for now, use [[je viens]] as a chunk. The little word changes like this:

- city: [[de]] → [[Je viens de Lyon.]]
- feminine country: [[de]], or [[d']] before a vowel → [[Je viens de France.]] [[Je viens d'Inde.]]
- masculine country: [[du]] (de + le) → [[Je viens du Maroc.]]
- plural country: [[des]] (de + les) → [[Je viens des États-Unis.]]

In conversation you'll also hear [[Je suis de Montréal]], with être. It means the same.

examples.fr: Je viens du Mexique, mais j'habite au Canada.
examples.en: I'm from Mexico, but I live in Canada.

blocks.body:
- **en + city:** [[J'habite en Montréal]] is wrong. Cities take [[à]]: [[J'habite à Montréal]].
- **en Canada:** [[le Canada]] is masculine, so say [[au Canada]].
- **Je habite:** the h is silent, so write and say [[j'habite]].
- **dans + city:** English “in” is not [[dans]] here. Say [[à Toronto]], not *dans Toronto*.
- **Forgetting the liaison:** [[nous‿habitons]] sounds like *nou-za-bi-TON*.

blocks.title: Why au and aux?
blocks.body: French never says *à le* or *à les*. They always fuse: **à + le = au**, **à + les = aux**. You'll meet these again with places in town. With feminine countries, French uses [[en]] and no article: [[en France]].

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: j'habite sounds like “zha-BEET”: the h is silent.

lines.en: They live in the United States.
lines.tip: Two z sounds: il-z‿habitent, o-z‿États-Unis. The -ent is silent.

blocks.explain: You hear [[au]] (an o sound), so it's the province. [[À Québec]] would be the city.
The *z* sound in [[ils‿habitent]] tells you it's plural. [[Il habite]] has no z.

blocks.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.

blocks.en: Karim lives in Montreal, in Quebec.

blocks.explain: Formal → [[vous habitez]]. [[Où habitez-vous ?]] is careful; [[Vous habitez où ?]] is everyday speech.

blocks.prompt: Sofia is Mexican, but she lives in Canada.
accept: Sofia est mexicaine, mais elle habite au Canada.
blocks.explain: Être for nationality ([[est mexicaine]]), habiter for where you live, and [[au]] for le Canada.
[[habitent]] ends in silent -ent, and [[États-Unis]] has a capital É and a hyphen.

blocks.prompt: I'm from Morocco, but I live in Montréal.
accept: Je viens du Maroc, mais j'habite à Montréal.
Je viens du Maroc mais j'habite à Montréal.
Je suis du Maroc, mais j'habite à Montréal.
Je suis du Maroc mais j'habite à Montréal.
blocks.hint: Morocco is masculine: de + le = du.
blocks.explain: [[Je viens du Maroc]] (de + le = du), then [[j'habite à]] + city.

blocks.prompt: A new neighbour asks about you. Say where you come from, your nationality, and where you live now (city and province or country). Then ask your neighbour where they live (use vous).

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Amira. Je viens du Maroc, je suis marocaine. Maintenant, j'habite à Sherbrooke, au Québec. Et vous, vous habitez où ?
models.en: Hello! My name is Amira. I'm from Morocco, I'm Moroccan. Now I live in Sherbrooke, in Quebec. And you, where do you live?

blocks.prompt: Write 3 or 4 sentences for a newcomers' forum: where you come from, where you live now, and where one other person lives (for example a friend).
checklist: en / au / aux + country or province
Il habite / Elle habite / Ils habitent…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je viens d'Inde. Maintenant, j'habite à Brampton, en Ontario. Mon ami Raj habite à Chicago, aux États-Unis. Et vous, vous habitez où ?
models.en: Hello! I'm from India. Now I live in Brampton, in Ontario. My friend Raj lives in Chicago, in the United States. And you, where do you live?

summary:
- Conjugate **habiter**: [[j'habite, tu habites, il/elle habite, nous habitons, vous habitez, ils/elles habitent]]
- Use [[à]] + city, [[en]] + feminine country, [[au]] + masculine country, [[aux]] + plural country
- Ask [[Tu habites où ?]] / [[Où habitez-vous ?]] and say where you're from with [[Je viens de…]]
- Tell [[au Québec]] (the province) from [[à Québec]] (the city)
